physics_goals.quote: The Telescope Array (TA) experiment is a hybrid UHECR observatory in the Northern Hemisphere located near Delta, Utah, USA
physics_goals.value: Determine the origin, composition and acceleration mechanism of ultra-high-energy cosmic rays using a hybrid surface-detector and fluorescence-telescope array in the Northern Hemisphere.

summary.plain: A cosmic-ray observatory in the Utah desert with over 500 ground detectors spread across 700 square kilometres and telescopes at three stations, watching for the rarest, most energetic particles from space; recently made four times bigger by the TAx4 extension.
summary.technical: Hybrid ultra-high-energy cosmic-ray observatory near Delta, Utah (~1400 m altitude): 507 plastic-scintillator surface-detector stations on a 1.2 km grid over ~700 km², plus 38 fluorescence telescopes at three sites (Middle Drum, Long Ridge, Black Rock Mesa). Taking data since 11 May 2008; extended since October 2019 by TAx4 (500 additional SDs on a 2.08 km grid, 12 new FD telescopes, target ~3000 km²).

unique_capabilities.quote: The Telescope Array (TA) is the largest ultra-high energy cosmic ray (UHECR) observatory in the Northern Hemisphere. ... At the highest energies, the TA×4 project expands the original TA aperture by a factor of four, with a target coverage of ∼3000 km2
unique_capabilities.value: The largest ultra-high-energy cosmic-ray observatory in the Northern Hemisphere; extended fourfold in area by the TAx4 project to gain statistics at the very highest energies.
